notes:
I read lines 1151-1217 directly. There are 43 stations, numbered 40-80, with 44, 48 and 55 each split into _a_ and _b_. There are no sub-headings, so I set coast to the section title, "EAST COAST OF ENGLAND". Even so, 78 Heligoland, 79 Casquets (Alderney) and 80 Hanois (Guernsey) are not on the English east coast. The list just includes them at the end.

How I recorded the rows:
- **Fragments:** I removed the leading indentation from each printed line but kept the spacing inside the text. That includes the missing space in "44_a_.*Teesmouth" and the uneven gaps after the numbers.
- **Numbers:** I dropped the full stop after each number ("40." becomes "40"; "44_a_." becomes "44_a_").
- **Final full stops:** I dropped the row-ending full stop from name, place and character. I kept it in other ("Nil return--no birds seen.", "returned by Major Russell.").
- **Wrapped text:** When a character or place runs onto a second line, I joined the two parts with a single space.
- **Place:** This holds the position text ("53 miles E.S.E. Spurn", "off Thames", "Goodwin Sands, 13 miles E. Deal").
- **Type:** This is only "Lighthouse" or "Lightvessel" where printed. Many lighthouses (40-47) have no type printed, so type is null for them.

Rows you may need to decide on:
- **45:** I kept "Whitby, High Light" as the name. "High Light" could also be read as a type or designation.
- **41:** "two lights" is in the character field ("two lights; white, revolving every 30 seconds"), not in other. I treated Coquet's "two white lights in same tower" the same way.
- **56:** "north end Hasborough Sound" comes after the light's character. I put it in place, not character.
- **66 Languard Point:** I put "Major Russell" in keepers because the list names him for the station ("returned by Major Russell"). His military rank suggests he was probably not a lightkeeper, but someone else who sent the return. Take him out of keepers if the roll should hold lightkeepers only. The full phrase is also in other.
- **No keepers otherwise:** The list names no other people. The other 42 stations have keepers [].

Marks: 39 stations have *. Four have no mark, so presumably no return: 63 Orfordness, 65 Cork, 71 Nore and 77 South Foreland. 43 Souter Point and 62 Lowestoft have * even though their rows say "Nil return--no birds seen". So * means a schedule came back, even an empty one. 44_b_ Teesmouth, 48_b_ Great Cotes, 55_a_ Northrepps and 78 Heligoland are just a name and a *, with no type or character. Teesmouth appears twice: 44_a_ is the No. 5 Buoy light-vessel, and 44_b_ has no type.

Spellings I copied without correcting:
- "Languard Point": the usual spelling is Landguard.
- "Hasborough": Happisburgh.
- "Hanoveaux Rocks": Hanois / Hanoveaux.
- "Newsand", "Lynndeeps", "South-sand Head", "East-side" and "Farne Inner": hyphens and word forms as printed.

Possible misprint: the Goodwin character (73) says "86 seconds dark". That may be a slip for 36, since Newarp (58) has the same three quick flashes and is "36 seconds in a minute dark". I kept 86.
